# sorted

> sorted is a Mac app that plugs into a shoot disk and makes the whole shoot searchable, in plain words, on the Mac, with nothing uploaded anywhere. Photos and video, people, plain-word search and delivery in one on-device app. Public beta.

## What it does

- Indexes a whole disk on the Mac: photos (JPEG, HEIC, RAW from Sony, DJI and others), 4K clips, drone footage. The disk is only ever read. The index lives on the Mac.
- Search in plain words, on photos and on video. A clip is broken into scenes and each scene is searchable. Examples: "sunset on the beach", "ring exchange", "man in a white shirt at a desk", "drone over the fort".
- Faces and people: every face in the stills is detected and grouped into people. Name a person once and every photo of them is one click away. Drop in one photo of someone and it finds every frame of them. When two groups might be the same person it asks once, Same or Different, and remembers.
- Categories it finds by itself: beach, ocean, boat, building, office, interview, night, food, sky, birds and animals, plus categories discovered from the shoot. Drone shots are a filter. Out of focus photos and clips can be filtered out.
- Deliver: select by person, category, search or hand-pick, then export to a folder on the Mac or any disk, or straight to a Google Drive folder (files go from the disk to Drive without a copy on the laptop). Or reorganise the whole disk into sorted folders by category and person, with an Undo.
- Nothing leaves the Mac. Fully offline. No account needed to sort. No upload, no telemetry. The one thing that leaves the Mac is what the user exports, where they say.

## What it is not

- Not an editor. It does not cut, colour or retouch. The edit happens in Premiere, Resolve, Lightroom, whatever the person already uses.
- Not a cloud service. There is no server doing the work.
- Not a chatbot. No language model is used anywhere. Two small on-device vision models: MobileCLIP (images and words in one space) and a face detector and recogniser (YuNet and SFace). They run on the Mac's own chip.
- Video faces: not yet. Faces are on photos; clips get the scene breakdown instead.
- Intel Macs: not supported in the beta. Needs an Apple silicon Mac (M1 to M4), macOS 14 or newer.

## Who it is for

Editors and post houses, designers, agencies and brand shoots, wedding photographers, cinematographers and DOPs, documentary crews, event and conference photographers, travel and lifestyle creators, real estate and architecture shoots, drone operators, archives and studios with old drives, and anyone with a big pile of photo and video data.

## Numbers (Apple M1, 8 GB, 2020 MacBook Air, the base model)

- 3,677 photos, 147 GB (Sony A7R V, 61 megapixel) indexed in 10 minutes 42 seconds.
- 955 items across 800 GB (630 photos, 325 4K clips, a documentary shoot) in 44 minutes 36 seconds.
- A 23 second DJI 4K clip scanned for scenes in 1.0 second with hardware decode (9.3 seconds without).
- 36 milliseconds per photo for the vision model, 83 milliseconds for the full pass including sharpness and faces.

## How it works

A small local program (Python) runs on the Mac and shows its interface in the browser (Chrome). It walks the disk, makes a thumbnail of every photo and a handful of frames of every clip, runs each through MobileCLIP to get a fingerprint of what is in it, runs a face detector on the stills, and stores all of that in one database on the Mac. A search turns the words into the same kind of fingerprint and finds the closest images.

## Status

Public beta, testing right now. Sign-ups on the landing page go to a waitlist. Next: a signed, notarised Mac app (drag to Applications, no Terminal), then a browser-only demo on 200 photos, then person search across shoots.
